title: Evaluating the fitness for purpose of the Serbian cadastral base map for use as a reference layer in municipal urban planning GIS

record.title: Evaluating the fitness for purpose of the Serbian cadastral base map for use as a reference layer in municipal urban planning GIS
record.abstract: Municipal urban planning in Serbia relies on the cadastral base map as a primary spatial reference, yet no systematic assessment of its fitness for planning-specific purposes has been conducted at a national scale. This paper develops a fitness-for-purpose assessment framework based on six criteria—positional accuracy, completeness, topological correctness, attribute currency, semantic alignment with planning ontology, and access and licensing constraints—and applies it to the cadastral datasets of eight municipalities of varying size and development pressure in the Vojvodina and Šumadija regions. Data were obtained directly from municipal cadastral offices under a research agreement. Positional accuracy (assessed by GNSS check survey, n=2 400 points) varied from 0.3 m to 2.1 m RMSE across municipalities. Topological correctness was below 95% in six of eight municipalities. Attribute currency was rated adequate in three municipalities. The paper concludes with a scoring matrix and identifies the principal bottlenecks for routine planning use.
